security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU implements the old (pre-fix) field width for the external interrupt vector table base address register, masking bits [5:2] (XLEN-6) instead of only bits [1:0] (XLEN-2). When the guest writes a vector table base address, QEMU's WARL masking incorrectly clears bits [5:2], forcing a 64-byte alignment instead of the correct 4-byte alignment. The guest OS reads back a truncated address and either places the IVT at an unintended location or fetches interrupt vectors from wrong addresses.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: extract64(val, 2, XLEN-2) or extract64(val, 6, XLEN-6) in ivt/xivt/eivt CSR write handlers; mask with ~0x3f vs ~0x3 for lower address bits of *_eivt registers; WARL field width of 58 vs 62 bits for the IVT base address field in AIA/ACLIC CSRs
security_spec.summary: Incorrect WARL field width masks bits [5:2] of external interrupt vector table base address, forcing 64-byte alignment instead of 4-byte, causing guest interrupt vectoring to fetch from wrong addresses

findings.finding: New spec-compliance check: when G-stage translation mode is BARE, MSIPTP mode MUST be OFF. Without this check, a misconfigured device context with IOHGATP.MODE=BARE and MSIPTP.MODE=FLAT would pass validation, potentially causing the MSI address check at line 289-295 to behave incorrectly — MSI GPA matching relies on G-stage translation being present (the MSI check only fires when !en_s, i.e., no first-stage, but the MSI page table walk itself requires G-stage to be configured). The fix correctly rejects this invalid combination per the RISC-V IOMMU spec device-context configuration checks.

Pre-existing check: T2GPA (translate-to-GPA) requires G-stage translation to be present (non-BARE). This correctly prevents a device context from requesting GPA passthrough while also requesting GPA translation. Operates independently of the new check above.
